Do the same for S05 (1955, not cousin Dale's 1956 / Putney), S07 (1971 / Brattleboro), and the K1_Q1 pairs on S01 (1912/Brattleboro), S02 (1931/Brattleboro), S04 (1948/Brattleboro), S06 (1967/Brattleboro), S08 (1969/Brattleboro) and S09 (1974/Brattleboro).

LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.problem: The brand sets the rule at 0.25 pt, which is 1/3 px. In a 1600 px JPEG that line is antialiased into a faint grey stroke, so no pixel will sample as #191613. The 'Archive Black #191613' part of the check cannot be judged by looking at the file. 'Thin ... hairline' also says the same thing twice.
LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.fix: Rewrite as one visible fact: If a rule appears beneath the sitter's name on “Family archive share image - hollis_scan_01” (share-hollis-scan-01.jpg), it is a single fine dark neutral hairline, not a heavy bar, a coloured line or a double line. Keep the Archive Black hex in evidence_reference only. Apply the same pattern to all nine files.

LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.problem: These checks ask the annotator to tell Archive Black #191613 from Ink Charcoal #33302B on Light-weight serif text in a JPEG. The place line is about 24 px and body text is about 12.7 px, with strokes 1 to 2 px wide. Antialiasing and JPEG compression move sampled values by more than the gap between the two colours, so an exact hex answer cannot be read from the pixels. The Ink Charcoal check (H049 and its equivalents) also combines two roles: the place and date line, plus any names or body line.
LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.fix: Use a relative check that can be seen, with the hex as the named reference. Name line: The sitter's name line on “…” (share-hollis-scan-01.jpg) is the darkest text in the caption, a near-black (Archive Black #191613). Place line: The place and date line on “…” (share-hollis-scan-01.jpg) is dark charcoal (Ink Charcoal #33302B), not grey and not a colour. Split the body role into a new check: If a names line or other caption body appears on “…” (share-hollis-scan-01.jpg), it is dark charcoal (Ink Charcoal #33302B), not grey.

LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.problem: 'Uses only #F5F1E9, #191613, #6F6B64, #D9D0C1 or #33302B' fails on every antialiased glyph edge in a JPEG, because edge pixels are blends of two colours, so read literally the check can never pass. A bare hex list is also hard for a designer to take in at a glance.
LANGUAGE, ATOMICITY AND OBSERVABILITY.fix: Rewrite as: Caption type, rules and keylines on “Family archive share image - hollis_scan_01” (share-hollis-scan-01.jpg) use only the archive neutrals (Paper White, Archive Black, Museum Grey, Linen, Ink Charcoal); no other hue, such as a colour or gold, appears. rejected.finding: FID-6: add a 'print sits level, edges parallel to the image edges' check to share images 01, 02, 03 and 06
rejected.why: No source requires the print to be level. The brief says only 'keep the whole print edge to edge, including its own border. Trim only the album page or scanner bed around it.' The existing deckled check says 'levelling the print is allowed', which permits levelling but does not require it. The trap's real consequence is that auto-level locks to the mount, so a rectangular trim can clip the tilted print's corners. The existing whole-print check H001 already guards that: 'shows the whole print ... edge to edge, its own border included; no part of the print is cropped away'. A level requirement would be invented. Instead I added coverage rule F13, which maps the trap to H001 on those four share images.
